title: Protocol to identify amino acids bound to tRNA by aminoacylation using mass spectrometry
protocol: Dissolve 6.0519 mg ATP in 100 μL DEPC-treated water to prepare a fresh ATP solution (c = 100 mM).
Mix the reagents listed in Table 1 in the specified order to obtain the reaction mix.
Incubate the reaction mix at 37°C for 3 hours.
Treat each reaction mix similarly for purification and digestion of aminoacylated tRNAArg.
Use a RNA purification kit to purify tRNAArg (non-aminoacylated or aminoacylated with arginine).
Follow the supplied manual for bacterial lysate preparation, starting from step 5.
Elute purified samples using a final volume of 50 μL.
Dissolve 6.6 mg EZ-Link Sulfo-NHS-Biotin in 100 μl HEPES buffer (120 mM HEPES, pH 8.0).
Add 50 μl of the biotinylation solution to each purified tRNAArg sample.
Incubate at 4°C for 12-14 hours.
Stain the gel with GelRed to visualize nucleic acids.
Visualize tRNAArg using GelRed staining.
Use Coomassie Blue G250 to stain the gel for protein visualization.
Identify the presence of streptavidin in the lanes where ArgRS is present.
Observe the band corresponding to tRNAArg in lanes where ArgRS is absent.
Notice a lower intensity band of free tRNAArg in lanes where ArgRS is present.
Detect an additional band representing biotinylated arginyl-tRNAArg when ArgRS is present.
Visualize streptavidin-bound biotinylated arginyl-tRNAArg using protein stain.
Digest tRNAArg.
Add 25 μL RNase A stock solution (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 1 mM EDTA, 50% Glycerol, 4 U/100 μL RNase A) and 5 μL of ammonium acetate solution (c = 220 mM) to each sample.
Incubate at 37°C for 2 h.
Use protein concentrators (Pierce Concentrator, PES, 3k MWCO, 0.5 mL; Thermo Fisher Scientific) for each sample.
Add 500 μL ultrapure water to pre-rinse the concentrator.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 5 min.
Remove ultrapure water from both chambers.
Add the sample to the concentrator.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 3 h.
Transfer filtrated fraction to a new vial and store at 4°C.
Define a separation method for the HPLC system.
Set the column oven temperature to 60°C.
Set the autosampler temperature to 7°C.
Equilibrate the column with 10% of eluent B at a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min until start of the measurement.
Use 20 μL of the sample for the measurement.
Use a linear gradient program with a constant flow rate of 0.5 mL/min for separation of the molecules in the sample.
Increase the percentage of eluent B from 10% to 30% over 10 min.
Increase the percentage of eluent B from 30% to 65% over 10 min.
Hold 65% of eluent B for 3 min.
Decrease the percentage of eluent B from 65% to 10% over 2 min.
Hold 10% of eluent B for 10 min.
Define a method for the mass spectrometer.
Use positive mode.
Set the mass range from 100 to 1000 Da.
Set the capillary voltage of the ESI to 4500 V with an End Plate Offset of −500 V.
Set the Nebulizer Gas pressure to 3.0 bar.
For the Dry Gas, use a flow rate of 8 L/min and a temperature of 250°C.
Acquire single scans with a scan time of 50 ms.
Calibrate the mass spectrometer using a NaTFA solution (c = 0.1 mg/mL) injected via syringe pump at 2 μL/min flow rate.
Acquire 64 scans with parameters listed for calibration.
Set lock masses: apply methyl stearate and hexakis(2,2-difluoroethoxy)phosphazene solutions to the ceramic slides of the lock mass reservoir as specified.
Calibrate the mass spectrometer again using the obtained spectrum.
Ensure accuracy of 1 ppm in the calibration; repeat steps if error is higher than acceptable limits.
Save the calibration settings.
Change the 6-port diverter valve back to HPLC mode on the 7T solariX.
Set number of scans to 1 and select serial mode.
Prepare two samples (digested tRNAArg, free form and aminoacylated with arginine).
Use 90 μL of the filtrated fraction.
Add 10 μL of HPLC grade ACN to obtain a final ACN concentration of 10% in the sample.
Add 0.1 μL of HPLC grade FA.
Vortex the sample for 10 s.
Briefly centrifuge the sample for 10 s.
Transfer the sample to 100 μL inserts placed in HPLC vials.
Place the HPLC vials into the autosampler pre-chilled at 7°C.
Create a sample list in Compass HyStar and select the written separation and measurement method as well as the saved calibration.
Perform a measurement on the samples.
Use a suitable program (Compass DataAnalysis, Bruker) for evaluating the obtained data.
Recalibrate the data using the lock masses.
Extract the ion chromatogram of the analyte.
Extract the ion chromatogram of biotinylated arginine (401.19655 m/z).
Analyze the extracted peaks.
Examine the compound spectrum.
Verify that the analyzed molecule is biotinylated arginine by measurement with a suitable standard.
Dissolve 3.3 mg EZ-Link Sulfo-NHS-Biotin in 50 μL HEPES buffer.
Add 50 μL of arginine working solution.
Incubate at 4°C for 12–14 h.
Measure the sample with the mass spectrometer without further purification.
